# Continual-ARC pattern procedures

Read only the section for a pattern whose grid signature matches. Treat each as a candidate rule to check against demonstrations, not as an assumption that overrides them.

## Noisy motif copies

For a noisy grid containing a distinctive single-color motif amid zeros and another background color, record the motif's colored-cell offsets from its bounding box. Search for translated copies whose motif positions all contain zeros, recoloring those matching positions with the motif color. Preserve every other cell, including the original motif and zeros/background at non-motif positions inside the bounding box. Do not assume flood-fill or neighbor propagation: test motif translations when the grid visually consists of noisy background plus one seed object. Use a small script to enumerate translations and construct output grids when manual scanning is error-prone. Account for seed shape, legal translations within bounds, and any rotation/reflection only if supported by demonstrations.

## Separator-tile classification

When full-width and full-height separator lines partition a grid into equal tiles and the output dimensions match the tile layout, map each tile to one output cell. Use demonstrations to identify which in-tile feature or count determines the output; do not assume every unusual cell or single marker is positive. For the task pattern with color-8 separators, 2×3 tiles containing mostly color 3 and occasional color 2, emit 1 for a tile with at least two 2s and 3 otherwise.

## Diagonal-stripe periods

For sparse colored diagonal markers on a zero field, identify the invariant of their parallel lines: constant row−column for down-right diagonals, or row+column for down-left diagonals. Demonstrations may show that the output fills the whole grid with a periodic color sequence indexed by that invariant. Use zero-based row/column coordinates and verify the sign convention against observed output: for down-right stripes, `column−row` indexes the phase; for down-left stripes, `row+column` does. Infer the smallest plausible period and color per phase by checking which candidate periods avoid assigning different colors to the same residue; use demo output to establish the complete mapping when available. Then color every cell from its phase, rather than preserving only the sparse markers. Verify several cells against each demonstrated line and ensure the resulting output reproduces every demo. Do not assume the marker positions alone give every residue's color; use output examples to establish the complete mapping.

## Missing edge continuations

When demonstrations show color 1 marking an absent continuation at a grid edge, compare repeated rows, bands, or motif copies to infer the expected continuation and affected cells. It may be a solid suffix or only selected motif-phase positions. Color only the confirmed missing continuation cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells. Check the candidate against every demo's changed and unchanged cells, and select repeated copies from that evidence—not from rightmost zeros or suffix length alone.
